verses.text: You were made alive when you were dead in transgressions and sins,
in which you once walked according to the course of this world, according to the prince of the power of the air, the spirit who now works in the children of disobedience;
among whom we also all once lived in the lusts of our flesh, doing the desires of the flesh and of the mind, and were by nature children of wrath, even as the rest.
But God, being rich in mercy, for his great love with which he loved us,
even when we were dead through our trespasses, made us alive together with Christ (by grace you have been saved),
and raised us up with him, and made us to sit with him in the heavenly places in Christ Jesus,
that in the ages to come he might show the exceeding riches of his grace in kindness toward us in Christ Jesus;
for by grace you have been saved through faith, and that not of yourselves; it is the gift of God,
not of works, that no one would boast.
For we are his workmanship, created in Christ Jesus for good works, which God prepared before that we would walk in them.
Therefore remember that once you, the Gentiles in the flesh, who are called “uncircumcision” by that which is called “circumcision”, (in the flesh, made by hands);
that you were at that time separate from Christ, alienated from the commonwealth of Israel, and strangers from the covenants of the promise, having no hope and without God in the world.
But now in Christ Jesus you who once were far off are made near in the blood of Christ.
For he is our peace, who made both one, and broke down the middle wall of partition,
having abolished in his flesh the hostility, the law of commandments contained in ordinances, that he might create in himself one new man of the two, making peace;
and might reconcile them both in one body to God through the cross, having killed the hostility thereby.
He came and preached peace to you who were far off and to those who were near.
For through him we both have our access in one Spirit to the Father.
So then you are no longer strangers and foreigners, but you are fellow citizens with the saints, and of the household of God,
being built on the foundation of the apostles and prophets, Christ Jesus himself being the chief cornerstone;
in whom the whole building, fitted together, grows into a holy temple in the Lord;
in whom you also are built together for a habitation of God in the Spirit.

footnotes.content: Paul doesn't soften it: we were *dead*. Not sick, not sleeping—dead in our sins and rebellion. But he opens with the hope: you *were* made alive. The Lord saw our tomb and opened it.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: He names it plain: the 'prince of the power of the air'—the spirit at work in rebellion. When we walked our own way, we walked in stride with powers that didn't have our good in mind. No wonder we wandered.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Paul includes himself—'we also all once lived.' Not pointing a finger from on high, but remembering his own life in the lusts of flesh and mind. Born to wrath like the rest, until grace found him.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Three words: *But God*. The whole gospel in two words. Rich in mercy, moved by love—the Lord saw our death and acted, not from duty but from the deep affection of His heart.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The parenthesis—'by grace you have been saved'—breaks in like a gasp of relief. We were dead, He made us alive *with Christ*. Not alone in the dark, but alive *in His resurrection*. That changes everything.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: From the grave to seated in heaven—in Christ. His exaltation became ours. When the Lord sat down at the right hand, believers sat down *with Him*. That's not a metaphor; it's our true position.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Future ages will behold our salvation and marvel at His grace. We become, across eternity, a living display of the kindness of Christ. What an honor—to be a trophy of grace.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Grace, faith, gift—not your doing. This verse has steadied my heart in my own stumbling. I cannot earn or win my salvation; it is given. That frees me to simply trust.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: No works, no boasting. The door to pride closes here. If I'm saved by grace, not by my merit, then I have nothing to brag about—only gratitude. That's a gentle rebuke and a relief.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: We're His *workmanship*—crafted by His hand. Not accidents; prepared by Him for good works He foreordained. Our days aren't random; He designed the very paths we walk.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Paul speaks to Gentiles, 'called uncircumcision'—a stigma under Jewish custom. But he tells them to *remember*. The old divisions that measured worth by bloodline or rite are about to dissolve.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Separate from Christ, strangers to the covenants, without God, without hope. That's the condition Paul describes—not as condemnation, but as the darkness before the dawn he's about to announce.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: But now—*in Christ Jesus*—the far-off are drawn near. The blood of Christ didn't just cover His own people; it opened the door to all who believe. Distance vanishes.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: He is our peace. Not a message or a doctrine, but a *person*. Christ broke the wall between Jew and Gentile, the very barrier that seemed eternal. When divisions crumble, He stands in the middle.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: He abolished in His flesh the hostility, the law of commandments. His body—broken on the cross—ended the system that divided. From two, He made one new man, and the peace was real.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Reconciled in one body to God through the cross. The Lord didn't mend the division and leave the hostility; He killed it. His blood reconciles us to the Father and to each other.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: He came and preached peace to both—to those far off and those near. The gospel goes out to all nations. One message, one peace, one Savior for every corner of the world.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Through Him, in one Spirit, we both have access to the Father. The great divide is gone. Jew and Gentile, bond and free, male and female—all come by one way, in one Spirit, to one Father.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: No longer strangers and foreigners—but *fellow citizens* and *household*. The language shifts from exile to belonging. We're not guests; we're family, built into God's own household.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Built on the apostles and prophets—the foundation laid by the apostles' witness to Christ. He is the chief cornerstone, the stone the builders rejected, now the cornerstone of the whole house.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The whole building grows into a holy temple. Not one stone, but all fitted together, growing toward completeness. The church—that's us—becomes a dwelling place of God's holiness.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: In whom you are built together for a habitation of God in the Spirit—and that echo reaches us still. Readers today hear it: the Lord builds us as His home. By His Spirit, He dwells *in us*. What a gift—to carry His presence.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight
